43.0.0.en: 1 The pure firmament is the pride of the heights, and the sight of heaven is a vision of glory. 2 The sun at its rising proclaims by its appearing. It is a wonderful instrument, the work of the Most High. 3 At its noontide it parches the land; who can stand before its heat? The sun is like one who blows a furnace, for what is made in the fire. 4 It burns the mountains threefold, and sends forth fiery vapors, and shines with rays that dazzle the eyes. 5 Great is the Lord who made it, at whose command it hastens on its course.

43.0.1.en: Jewish writers and astronomers among some nations, such as the Pharaohs and the Greeks, were concerned to explain in various ways the phenomena of the heavenly bodies and the atmosphere, but what occupied Ben Sira was how these phenomena bore witness to the surpassing wisdom of the Creator. Very briefly, Sirach brings out the role of the sun in creation.

43.0.2.en: a. Its appearing radiates with joy [1-2]; the secret of its joy is the need of the earth, with its plants, animals and man, for it.

43.1.0.en: b. It shines upon the earth and dries it [3].

43.2.0.en: c. It shines upon the mountains and makes them like a furnace of fire, and upon the waters and sends forth vapors [4]; the eye cannot fix upon it and is darkened, whereas without it we cannot see what is around us.

43.2.1.en: d. It seems to be moving from its rising to its setting.

43.2.2.en: Ben Sira begins by speaking of it as it appears on the horizon, as though it dwelt there and ran from the east to the west. He sees it at its rising as though God sends it to mankind to announce the beginning of a new day. It calls the believer to constant movement and work until the day of his setting from the temporal world. Similar teaching about the sun is found: "In them hath he set a tabernacle for the sun, which is as a bridegroom coming out of his chamber, and rejoiceth as a strong man to run a race. His going forth is from the end of the heaven, and his circuit unto the ends of it: and there is nothing hid from the heat thereof" (Ps 19:4-7).

43.2.3.en: The joy of the heavenly height is the firmament of purity, and the structure of heaven in the vision of His glory [1].

43.2.4.en: The firmament is called "heaven" from the use of this word for what is lofty and high above the earth[1]. This firmament divides the waters that are above, that is, the clouds, from the waters that are below, that is, the seas and oceans. Besides its literal fulfillment, this division carried a spiritual meaning touching the life of man. If the spiritual man receives at the outset the breaking forth of the divine radiance in his inner depths, it is fitting for him to bear the firmament that divides between waters and waters, so that he receives the waters of the Holy Spirit from above that give life (Jn 4:14) and rises above the waters that are below, that is, in the depths, which are inhabited by Leviathan, the ancient serpent, and the sea monster that wars against the human soul (Rev 12:7; 20:3). Whoever enjoys the release into the firmament distinguishes between the grace of the Spirit and the deceptions of the Evil One.

43.2.5.en: The sun at its appearing announces its shining; what a wonderful instrument, the work of the Most High [2].

43.2.6.en: The Pharaohs called the sun the god Ra, and the Greeks the god Apollo; here Ben Sira affirms that it is the work of the Most High.

43.2.7.en: v Do we not marvel, astonished, at the structure of the sun? For it appears to the sight a small body, yet it carries a mighty power. It rises from the east and sends its rays to the west. And as the Psalmist described its rising at dawn, saying: "As a bridegroom coming out of his chamber" (Ps 19:5). He has pictured for us its splendor and the mildness of its heat at the beginning of its rising for men, so that when noontide comes we often flee from gazing upon it. Its rising is a delight to all; it is like the bridegroom! Consider also its ordering (or rather, the ordering of God, the Maker of its work), how it appears high in summer, when the day is long, giving men an opportunity to work, and in winter the cold increases and the night lengthens for the rest of men... It also contributes to the fruits of the produce of the earth![2]

43.2.8.en: St. Cyril of Jerusalem v Lift up your eyes to heaven, like him who said: "Unto thee lift I up mine eyes, O thou that dwellest in the heavens" (Ps 123:1). Look to the Sun of righteousness, for when the commandments of the Lord, which represent the brightest of the stars, direct you, you will have watchful eyes. Do not allow the eyes (of the soul) to slumber, nor the eyelids of the eye to rest (Ps 132:4), until the commandments lead you continually. He says: "Thy law is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path" (Ps 119:105).

43.2.9.en: Truly, if you never sleep while you are at the helm that steers life... you will receive the help of the Spirit, who leads you in a gentle breeze and in safety full of peace until you cross over and reach the calm harbor in stillness and without any harm to you, by the will of God[3].

43.2.10.en: St. Basil the Great At noon it dries the earth; who can endure its burning heat? [3]

43.2.11.en: The man who kindles the furnace works in burning heat, and the sun burns the mountains threefold, sends forth burning vapors, and sends out its rays so that the eyes are darkened [4].

43.3.0.en: Great is the Lord who made it, and at His command it hastens on its course [5].

43.3.1.en: St. Cyril of Jerusalem sees that the sun at its setting glorifies God, since man rests from the toil of the day, as he says: [Let no one say that the Creator of light is not the Creator of darkness, but remember what is written in Isaiah! I am God, "I form the light, and create darkness" (Isa 45:7). Why are you troubled at this, O man? Why are you displeased at the opportunity given you for rest?! Would a servant be permitted rest by his master if the darkness did not compel him to rest of necessity?! After the weariness of the day we are refreshed by night, and we rise in the morning with our strength renewed after the burdens of the day's labors, thanks to the rest of the night. What is more profitable to man than the night for attaining wisdom?! For in it we often meditate on the works of God, and in it we read the divine sayings and understand them, and in it we especially compose our minds to chant Psalmody and prayer! Does this not happen at night?![4]]

43.4.0.en: 6 And the moon, in all its appointed phases, is the announcement of the seasons and a sign of the age. 7 From the moon comes the sign of the feast. It is a luminary that wanes at its fullness. 8 The month is named after it, and in its changing it increases wonderfully. 9 There is on high an encampment of a host shining in the firmament of heaven.

43.4.1.en: The moon, which draws its light from the sun, has its own role. The sun announces every morning a new day, and with every setting is a call to rest from the struggle of work, while the moon appears changing, determines the seasons and months, announces the feasts, shines in the heights, and pours out joy amid the darkness of the night.

43.4.2.en: The sun is like a furnace and the moon is like a lamp, and neither the one nor the other can be dispensed with! The moon is the sign of the changing of the seasons, especially in the religious calendar of the Jews (Ex 12:2; Ps 104:19).

43.4.3.en: Origen says: [Christ is the light of the world who illumines the Church with His light. As the moon draws its light from the sun and so lights up the darkness, so the Church draws light from Christ to shine upon those who are in the darkness of ignorance[5].] He also says: [The higher we rise to look upon the sunrise from the heights, the better the splendor and the warmth are. So the more our thought ascends and is lifted up to Christ, the nearer it draws to the brightness of His radiance, and we are enlightened by His light in greater splendor and beauty. And as He Himself says: "Turn ye unto me, saith the LORD of hosts, and I will turn unto you" (Zech 1:3)... If we are able to go up with Him to the top of the mountain like Peter, James and John, we are enlightened by the light of Christ and by the voice of the Father Himself[6].]

43.5.0.en: And He also made the moon to determine the change of the seasons[7], to announce the times and as an everlasting sign [6].

43.5.1.en: From the moon appears the sign of the feast, that light which wanes as it completes its course [7].

43.5.2.en: By its name the month is called, and in its phases it increases in a wonderful way.

43.6.0.en: And it is a vessel[8] that dwells in the heights[9]:

43.6.1.en: It is a lamp for the hosts on high, shining in the firmament of heaven [8].

43.7.0.en: The moon moves according to the order that the Lord set for it, and as for its faithfulness in determining the seasons, this is understood among the peoples whose calendar is based on the cycle of the moon, such as the Arabs, the Jews and others (Ps 89:38; 104:19), like the beginning of months (Gen 1:14); it is the beginning of the month for the Jews, and is called by the Jews the head of the month (the New Moon), and it is a symbol of stability (Ps 72:5); it determines precisely the beginning of the feasts such as the Passover and the harvest, and the Book of Numbers mentions how to depend on the moon in appointing such occasions (Num 28:11-15)[10].

43.8.s.en: 3. The stars, the rainbow and the snow glorify the Creator

43.8.0.en: 10 There is the beauty of heaven and the glory of the stars, and a shining world, and the Lord in the heights. 11 At the word of the Holy One they stand to carry out His judgments, and no weariness takes hold of them in their watches. 12 Look upon the rainbow, and bless its maker. Its splendor is exceedingly beautiful. 13 It girds heaven with a girdle of glory, and the hands of the Most High stretch it out. 14 At His command He hastens the snow, and hurls the lightnings of His judgment. 15 And by Him the treasures are opened, and the clouds fly like birds. 16 By His greatness He strengthens the clouds; and the hailstones are broken in pieces. 17 At His glances the mountains are shaken, and at His will the south wind blows. 18 At the voice of His thunder the earth travails, at the storm of the north and the whirlwind. 19 He scatters the snow as birds flying down alight, and its descent is like the alighting of locusts. 20 The eye marvels at the beauty of its whiteness, and the heart is astonished at its raining. 21 And He pours out the frost like salt upon the earth, and when it freezes it becomes like the points of stakes. 22 The cold north wind blows, and the water freezes. The ice settles upon every gathering of waters, and clothes the waters with a breastplate. 23 It devours the mountains and burns the wilderness, and consumes the green like fire. 24 The mist hastens and heals everything, and the dew coming after the heat restores gladness.

43.8.1.en: The stars in their countless numbers stand like soldiers amid the darkness, serving the will of God [9-10]. They urge mankind to cease worshiping idols and to return to the Maker, the Creator. The greatness of the sun, the moon and the stars brings out the power and wisdom of the Almighty Creator, and rebukes those who worship the beautiful creation instead of its Creator.

43.9.0.en: The rainbow [11-12] is not mentioned in the six days of creation, but appeared as a sign of the covenant and of the Creator's care for mankind (Gen 9). Here he speaks of it as encircling heaven with a glorious arc, and the hands of the Most High stretch it out [2].

43.10.0.en: He speaks of the snow and the lightning [13]; the snow comes down slowly so that it does not harm men, and He allows the lightning to appear and quickly vanish, so that it does not harm the eyes; while the clouds move in the air like birds [14]. Wonderful is the Lord in His plan for us: He makes the clouds light, as though they fly in the air, and the hail heavy, falling to the earth.

43.10.1.en: The glory of the stars is the beauty of heaven, a radiant adornment in the heights of the Lord [9].

43.10.2.en: v Behold, the creatures in the diversity of their forms chant Your praise, and I open my mouth to praise Your might.

43.10.3.en: Behold, the days and the nights within their bounds are opened and closed to spread Your report in all the earth.

43.10.4.en: The evenings and the mornings awaken men by their watches and their seasons to praise You with discernment.

43.10.5.en: The summers and the winters teach the earth by their changes and their courses that You alter its seasons.

43.10.6.en: The cold and the heat, which go and come for the ordering, tell how skilled You are in Your works.

43.10.7.en: The hours of the day and the four watches of the night all send up distinct praises to Your creative power...

43.10.8.en: All the dry land and the earth and its mountains with their hills praise You, and You bear them up lest they fall.

43.10.9.en: Behold, the heavens declare Your glory by their natures, and the firmament shows the work of Your hands: how mighty You are!

43.10.10.en: Behold the great tent that Your creative power wove, and spread out, stretched and standing above all directions, and it is filled with Your praise.

43.10.11.en: The sun and the moon, their rays and their risings, awaken the world with the great procession of Your praise[11].

43.10.12.en: St. Jacob of Serugh At the words of the Holy One they stand according to His judgment[12], and weariness has no power over them in their watches [10].

43.10.13.en: St. Cyril of Jerusalem says: [It would have been more fitting for them to be astonished and marvel not only at the order of the sun and the moon, but at the exact arrangements of the stars and the appearance of each star in its due time. From its appearing summer and winter are known, and some of them announce the time of planting and others announce the beginning of sailing. For a man sitting in his ship sails among boundless waves, guiding his ship by looking to the stars. And as Holy Scripture says of these things, "and let them be for signs, and for seasons... and years" (Gen 1:14), and not for the sake of astrology and idle tales[13].]

43.10.14.en: Look upon the rainbow, and bless its maker, for its radiance is exceedingly beautiful [11].

43.10.15.en: The rainbow is like a jewel that adorns creation. In the Book of Revelation a rainbow like unto an emerald appears around the throne (Rev 4:3). The Lord gave the rainbow as a sign of His covenant with man, that He would not drown the earth with a flood again. With this divine pastoral work, the rainbow glorifies God with its splendor, exceedingly beautiful.

43.10.16.en: It goes around heaven with its glorious arc, and the hands of the Most High determine its course [12].

43.10.17.en: At His command the snow falls, and He hastens the lightning by His judgment [13].

43.10.18.en: He describes God's care for creation in the following:

43.10.19.en: a. Through commands: "At His command the snow falls" [13].

43.11.0.en: b. Through His appearing: "At His appearing the mountains are shaken" [16].

43.11.1.en: c. Through His will: "At His will the south wind blows" [16].

43.12.0.en: d. Through sprinkling or scattering: "He scatters the snow as birds fall" [18].

43.13.0.en: e. Through pouring: "He pours out the frost like salt upon the earth" [19].

43.14.0.en: f. Through destroying: "He destroys the mountains and burns the wilderness" [21].

43.15.0.en: g. Through ordering: "According to His purpose He subdued the great deep" [23].

43.16.0.en: h. Through His word: "By His word all things are done" [26].

43.16.1.en: Therefore the storehouses are opened, and the clouds fly like birds [14].

43.16.2.en: In his love for beautiful nature, Ben Sira sees the clouds moving in the heights like birds singing in exultation [14]. And when the hail falls like little grains and covers the mountains so that they all become like a white carpet [16], the eye marvels at the beauty of its whiteness, and the mind is astonished at its falling [18].

43.16.3.en: He also sees in the rains and the dew that they transform the earth, which suffers from intense scorching heat, into a fertile land, delightful with fruits and flowers.

43.16.4.en: St. Cyril of Jerusalem says: [Who stored up the air in the clouds, and bound them to carry the waters of the rains, so that they come golden in color (Job 37:22) from the south, now in one order, and now in the form of many circles and varied shapes?! "Who can number the clouds in wisdom?" (Job 38:37), since it is said in Job: Does He "know the separation of the clouds?!" (Job 37:16) LXX. Who is He "that bringeth the wind out of his treasuries" (Ps 135:7), and as we said before: "Who hath begotten the drops of dew? Out of whose womb came the ice?!" (cf. Ps 135:7; Job 38:28) For their matter is water, and their power is like stone! At one time the water becomes snow like wool (cf. Ps 147:16), and at another He scatters it as frost like ashes, and a third time it becomes a stony substance. He rules the water as He wills. The nature of water is one, but its work is manifold in power, for it makes in the vine wine that makes glad the heart of man, and in the olive oil that makes his face to shine, and in bread it strengthens man's heart (Ps 104:15), and it is found in all kinds of fruit that God created[14].]

43.16.5.en: By His greatness He thickens the clouds, and the hail is shattered into pieces [15].

43.16.6.en: At His appearing the mountains are shaken, and at His will the south wind blows [16].

43.16.7.en: The sound of His thunder shakes the earth, and so do the storm of the north and also the whirlwind [17].

43.16.8.en: He scatters the snow as birds fall, and it descends as the locust falls.

43.16.9.en: The eye marvels at the beauty of its whiteness, and the mind is astonished at its falling like rain [18].

43.16.10.en: He pours out the frost like salt upon the earth, and when it freezes it becomes like heads of thorns [19].

43.16.11.en: The cold north wind blows, and the ice freezes upon the water, and settles upon every gathering of waters, and clothes the waters as with a breastplate [20].

43.16.12.en: The Lord Himself calls us to flee from the land of the north, as from Babylon, to set out for Zion, where the Lord comes and dwells in our midst (Zech 2:6-10).

43.16.13.en: The blowing of the cold north wind: since the north winds coming upon the Middle East region are marked by coldness, it points to the attack of the devil and sin upon the believer, to take from him the warmth of the Spirit; it is said: "And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold" (Mt 24:12).

43.16.14.en: In the visions of Zechariah the prophet, those in Babylon were called to flee from the land of the north to return to Jerusalem, the city of God (south of Babylon). "Ho, ho, flee from the land of the north, saith the LORD" (Zech 2:6). St. Didymus the Blind comments on this call, saying: [He made clear to where and in what city salvation is possible for those fleeing from the harsh cold of the north wind... It is Zion, the holy land, where those who formerly dwelt in it can flee from Babylon in safety... And since the name "Babylon" means confusion, every person who is confused in mind is counted a Babylonian, which must be avoided, by the desire to flee to Zion where the praises of God are sung, for it is the place fitting for praising God, "Sing praises to the LORD, which dwelleth in Zion" (Ps 9:11).]

43.16.15.en: v We have been commanded to be fervent in spirit (Rom 12:11); this shows that the word of God is a blazing fire. Jeremiah heard from him who gave him the divine revelation: "Behold, I have put my words in thy mouth" (Jer 1:9). And since God is a fire (Deut 4:24; Heb 12:29), it is fitting for the saints to be aflame with the Spirit of God.

43.16.16.en: (The wicked) are without doubt cold in their love for Him; truly the Lord says: "And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold." And all those who symbolize the opposing power in the Holy Scriptures are always cold. Satan is in truth called a serpent and a dragon (Rev 12:9; 20:2); who are colder than these? It is said of the dragon that he rules in the waters (cf. Ezek 32:2). And in another place He says: "The Lord shall punish with the holy sword the dragon, the fleeing serpent... and shall slay the dragon there" (cf. Isa 27:1). And in another passage: "And though they be hid from my sight in the bottom of the sea, thence will I command the serpent, and he shall bite them" (Amos 9:3).

43.16.17.en: And in the Book of Job this creature was called king over all the beings that are in the water (Job 41:25). The prophet declares that evils come from the north, especially upon those who dwell on the earth (Jer 1:14). And the north wind is referred to in the Holy Bible as cold, as it is said in Wisdom: "The icy north wind." Without question it is fitting for us to refer these to Satan[15].

43.16.18.en: Origen v To make the flight easier, he made clear where and in what city salvation is within the reach of those fleeing from the cold, piercing wind (Sir 43:20; Prov 27:16). It is Zion, the holy place, where its former inhabitants from the daughters of Babylon can flee to it in safety[16].

43.16.19.en: St. Didymus the Blind He (the Lord) destroys the mountains, and burns the wilderness, and dries up the tender grass like fire [21].

43.16.20.en: The mist restores them all quickly, and the falling dew refreshes from the heat [22].

43.17.s.en: 4. The great deep glorifies the Creator

43.17.0.en: 25 By His word He calmed the deep, and made islands to grow in it. 26 Those who sail the sea tell of its terror. We hear it with our ears and marvel. 27 There are the wonderful and strange works: all kinds of animals, the creatures of the whales.

43.17.1.en: The ancient Israelites were accustomed to look upon the seas as terrifying (Ps 107:23-32; Jon 1:4-16), while stressing God's power in overcoming the destructive power of the seas. Here Ben Sira brings out the beauty of the islands surrounded by the waters of the seas, with diverse and beautiful fish, and also sea monsters.

43.17.2.en: According to His purpose[17] He calmed the great deep, and caused islands to grow in it [23].

43.17.3.en: St. Cyril of Jerusalem says: [In this great, wide sea live creatures without number (Ps 104:25); who can describe the wonder of the fish that live in it?! Who can imagine the greatness of the whales and the nature of the amphibious animals: how they live now upon solid land and again amid the waters?![18]]

43.17.4.en: And those who sail the sea recount its dangers, and we marvel at the reports that our ears hear: [24]

43.17.5.en: For there are strange, wonderful works, and diverse varied living beings, and created orders of huge sea monsters [25].

43.17.6.en: St. Cyril of Jerusalem says: [Who among men knows even the names of all the wild beasts?! Or who can distinguish the physiology of each of them accurately? If you do not know of the wild beasts even their mere names, how do you understand their Creator?![19]]

43.18.0.en: 28 By Him the end is brought to success, and by His word all things consist. 29 We multiply words and yet fall short, and the sum of what is said is that He is the all. 30 What can we do to glorify Him, for He is great above all His works. 31 Fearful is the Lord and very great, and His power is wonderful. 32 Exalt the Lord in His glorification as much as you can; still He is higher. 33 Bless the Lord and exalt Him as much as you are able; for He is greater than all praise. 34 Be extravagant in exalting Him according to your strength. Do not grow weary, for you will never attain to Him. 35 Who has seen Him that he may tell? And who can magnify Him as He is? 36 And there are many hidden things greater than these; for what we have seen of His works is little. 37 The Lord has made all things, and has given wisdom to the godly.

43.18.1.en: Because of Him (the Lord) His messenger prospers in his journey, and by His word all things work together [26].

43.18.2.en: The Apostle Paul presents similar expressions, saying: "For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible... all things were created by him, and for him" (Col 1:16).

43.18.3.en: We can multiply words without reaching the goal, and the sum of our words is this: "He is the all" [27].

43.18.4.en: God is omnipresent, present in every place and at all times; He is in all things, and He is above all things; He is the all.

43.18.5.en: v When we come to You, this many speaking that we do without comprehension will be abolished, and You are the One who remains. You are all in all (1 Cor 15:28), and without ceasing we shall say one thing, we shall praise You in the One, we who become one in You[20].

43.18.6.en: St. Augustine How can we praise Him as is fitting?

43.18.7.en: For He is greater than all His works [28].

43.18.8.en: v As we bend our knees with good reverence before the Maker of the worlds, I mean the world of sense and of thought, what is seen and what is unseen, you glorify God with a holy tongue that speaks of what is good, and lips that are not silent, and a heart that does not grow weary, saying: "O LORD, how manifold are thy works! in wisdom hast thou made them all" (Ps 104:24); to You belong honor and glory and majesty from now through all the ages. Amen[21].

43.19.0.en: St. Cyril of Jerusalem Fearful is the Lord and very great, and wonderful is His power [29].

43.19.1.en: Glorify the Lord and magnify Him as much as you can, for He is above all this.

43.20.0.en: Magnify Him with all your strength, and do not grow weary, for you will not glorify Him sufficiently [30].

43.20.1.en: v The subject of our meditation in this present life must be the praises of God, because the perpetual loftiness of our coming life is praise of Him, and no one can prepare for the life to come unless he practices it himself now.

43.20.2.en: Our praise is marked by joy, and our prayers by sighing... Concerning these two matters, one is practiced in the trials and afflictions of this life, and the other pertains to the life to come, in eternal rest and heaven[22].

43.20.3.en: St. Augustine Who has seen Him that he may describe Him?

43.21.0.en: And who is able to magnify Him truly as He is? [31]

43.21.1.en: v In truth, by what understanding can a person comprehend God if he cannot understand his own mind, by which he knows God?[23]

43.22.0.en: St. Augustine Yet there are many hidden things greater than these, for we have seen but little of His works [32].

43.22.1.en: As knowledge advances and our knowledge of God's creation increases, we realize that we are on the shore of knowledge, and humanity remains, until the day of its meeting with the Creator face to face, confessing its inability to comprehend all the mysteries of creation and the extent of the Creator's care for it. This inability gives us a thirst not only for knowledge but also for the Creator, all-wise and all-loving.

43.23.0.en: For the Lord has made all things, and has given wisdom to the godly (those who fear the Lord) [33].

43.23.1.en: If visible and invisible nature praises God by its obedience to the law that God set for it, then man, who lost the image of God and is no longer in His likeness because of sin, praises God by recovering the lost image and enjoying the wisdom of God, which is a matter of God's delight!

43.24.s.en: Grant me to join the choir of those who praise!

43.24.0.en: v Arise, O Holy One, in our hearts, and renew our souls, that we may join joyfully the choir of those who praise, and our hearts, minds and emotions be drawn toward contemplating You.

43.24.1.en: v All creation praises You by its submission to the law that You set for it.

43.24.2.en: Grant us to join even this irrational creation, and in the spirit of obedience to praise Your holy name.

43.24.3.en: It praises You by working in silence!

43.24.4.en: Grant us to praise You when You shine with Your light in us, to praise You by our silence together with the purity of our hearts!

43.24.5.en: Our inner man praises You, by Your Kingdom which You establish within us!

43.24.6.en: It is the work of Your Holy Spirit.
